speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: On the orders of the day:

speakeroldname: Hon. George H. Hees (Minisier of Transport):
speakerposition: Minister of Transport
maintopic: TRANSPORT
subtopic: STATEMENT ON ALLEGED USE OF DEPARTMENTAL FACILITIES IN GREAT LAKES PILOTS STRIKE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, yesterday the hon. members for Welland (Mr. McMillan) and Port Arthur (Mr. Fisher) inquired regarding a newspaper report to the effect that radio communications facilities belonging to the Department of Transport were being used to break the strike of the great lakes pilots association.
According to my information this report is not accurate, as I am advised by my officials that radiotelephone facilities at the entrance to the Welland canal have always been used as a means of communication with shipping for a variety of purposes, to assist both the canal operators in their control procedures and planning, and to assist the ships. Messages passed within the capacity of the system deal with a variety of subjects, such as expected times of arrival of vessels, delivery of provisions and other matters associated with ship operations.
Whatever use is being made of these facilities at present is simply a continuation of a service which has been in use for a number of years.

maintopic: TRANSPORT
subtopic: STATEMENT ON ALLEGED USE OF DEPARTMENTAL FACILITIES IN GREAT LAKES PILOTS STRIKE
speechtext: A supplementary question on the same subject addressed to the Minister of Labour. Can the minister tell us whether the Department of Labour has determined if this dispute between the great lakes pilots association and the shipping federation of Canada is in fact a strike and properly under the jurisdiction of the department.

speakeroldname: Hon. Ellen L. Fairclough (Acting Minister of Labour):
speakerposition: Minister of Citizenship and Immigration
maintopic: TRANSPORT
subtopic: STATEMENT ON ALLEGED USE OF DEPARTMENTAL FACILITIES IN GREAT LAKES PILOTS STRIKE
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, as I understand the situation there is no contract; it is a rather loose arrangement, and therefore cannot properly be considered to be a matter under the jurisdiction of the department.

maintopic: TRANSPORT
subtopic: STATEMENT ON ALLEGED USE OF DEPARTMENTAL FACILITIES IN GREAT LAKES PILOTS STRIKE
speechtext: A further question, then, to the Minister of Transport. In view of the statement just made by the minister responsible for the Department of Labour, can the minister go ahead with his attempts to mediate this dispute now that it has been determined that it does not come under the Department of Labour?

speakerposition: Minister of Transport
maintopic: TRANSPORT
subtopic: STATEMENT ON ALLEGED USE OF DEPARTMENTAL FACILITIES IN GREAT LAKES PILOTS STRIKE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, as I advised the house some time ago, the Department of

Transport has offered on numerous occasions to provide whatever facilities would be considered useful in helping to end the difficulty which exists between the shipping federation and the pilots. At any time both sides decide that we can provide some assistance in this matter we shall be glad to co-operate in whatever way we are requested to assist.

speechtext:
I should like to direct a question to the Prime Minister. Would he care to comment on the Canadian Press dispatch in this morning's Montreal Gazette which is as follows:
Prime Minister Diefenbaker said tonight the government plans to take "comprehensive action" to combat unemployment "regardless of deficits in the national budget."
Does this mean new action to combat unemployment, and is the Prime Minister forecasting a deficit in the budget?

speakeroldname: Right Hon. J. G. Diefenbaker (Prime Minister):
speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: LABOUR CONDITIONS
subtopic: UNEMPLOYMENT
speechtext: In that speech, Mr. Speaker, I set forth something of the initial reasons for the degree of unemployment that existed when we came into power, something of the courses of action already followed and then, with a degree of modest pride, I set forth some of the courses already taken and stated that we intend to continue these courses as well as long-range policies of national development and the like to the end that this problem be met regardless of cost.

maintopic: LABOUR CONDITIONS
subtopic: UNEMPLOYMENT
speechtext: I have a supplementary question, Mr. Speaker. Would the Prime Minister comment on the particular part of the quotation which reads "regardless of deficits in the national budget"? Are those remarks correct?

speakerposition: Speaker of the House of Commons
maintopic: LABOUR CONDITIONS
subtopic: UNEMPLOYMENT
speechtext: Order. The hon. member knows that it is not proper to ask the Prime Minister to divulge the contents of the budget in advance of its presentation in the house.

maintopic: LABOUR CONDITIONS
subtopic: UNEMPLOYMENT
speechtext: On the point you have raised, Mr. Speaker, I wish to point out that these words are in a direct quotation. They are taken from a speech the Prime Minister made yesterday at a meeting of the Canadian Manufacturers Association. speakerposition: Speaker of the House of Commons
maintopic: LABOUR CONDITIONS
subtopic: UNEMPLOYMENT

maintopic: LABOUR CONDITIONS

speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: LABOUR CONDITIONS
subtopic: UNEMPLOYMENT
speechtext: The only comment I can make is that those words are perfectly explanatory, that regardless of the cost and the resulting expenditures that may have to be made and that have already been made, we intend to meet the situation.

speakerposition: topic
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: On the orders of the day:

speakeroldname: Hon. L. B. Pearson (Leader of the Opposition):
speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: I should like to ask the Prime Minister whether he would care to comment on a resolution approved unanimously yesterday at a meeting of the Canadian Federation of Mayors and Municipalities calling for federal action on unemployment, and indicating that the public works program outlined already by the government would not take care of immediate employment needs.

speakeroldname: Right Hon. J. G. Diefenbaker (Prime Minister):
speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
As a comment may I say that is an opinion of an organization, if correctly quoted. We have set forth the situation in this country. We have pointed out that the public works program is one of the phases 57071-3-574
Inquiries of the Ministry with which this government has proceeded in order to meet the situation.
According to economists there are several means that should be adopted. One is to provide additional consumer monetary assistance in order that the consumer may be able, by the expansion of his income, to make purchases, thereby improving the general situation. The second is by a public works program. The third is by action in the reduction of taxes. All three courses of action have been followed. In no case has any one of these three legs of the tripod, as it were, for recovery been followed in its entirety. Each complements the other. None of the three by itself is recognized by economists as sufficient to meet the situation.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
May I ask
the Prime Minister a supplementary question. In the light of the resolution unanimously passed by the Canadian Federation of Mayors and Municipalities as mentioned by the Leader of the Opposition, and the Prime Minister's understandable interest in the problem, it might be of interest to the country if the Prime Minister could meet the federation not in September but perhaps much earlier than that.

speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: As far as I am concerned, Mr. Speaker, there has been no suggestion with regard to an earlier meeting. The general reactions I received to the suggestion that we should call the municipalities together in the situation already detailed by me were accepted as a fair basis for the consideration of this and other related problems; and it was concluded that the month of September, or the period following the month of September, after the trade conference had been concluded, would be a sufficiently early date to meet the requirements of the municipalities for the consideration of their problems as well as any other matters that might arise.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: I wonder if I might ask the Prime Minister a supplementary question arising out of the very important statement he has made regarding the three methods by which unemployment can be dealt with. Does this very important statement also cover the matter of deficiency payments to western producers?

speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, what I said a while ago amounted simply to a recapitulation of the policy carried out by this government in order to help the farmers and make cash advances available to them, under the heading of expanding consumer credit. In so far as the question of deficiency payments is concerned, this is a matter which is receiving consideration. Further than that I cannot go at this time.

Supply-Public Works SUPPLY
The house in committee of supply, Mr. Rea in the chair.
DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS 328. General administration, $8,536,892.

speakeroldname: Hon. Howard C. Green (Minister of Public Works):
speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, the estimates of the Department of Public Works are, in the main, of such a nature that they call for discussion as the items themselves come up for consideration. However, I should like to make a few general remarks today with regard to the department.
It is one of the oldest departments in the government service, and it has had a long record of accomplishment of works across the country. In recent months, however, it has faced much heavier responsibilities than in ordinary times. For many months now the officials of the department not only in Ottawa but across the country have been extremely busy working on projects which will give additional employment, and I am sure hon. members will realize this as I go on with my remarks.
The department has a function of its own in connection with its own work and, in addition, it does a great deal of work for other departments of government. Falling within our own jurisdiction are such projects as public buildings, harbours, bridges, a certain amount of highway work, more particularly the federal share in the trans-Canada highway and the construction of highways in the national parks, which latter job is really done for the Department of Northern Affairs and National Resources. There are many other works, including dredging, but these are the main ones carried on by the department as part of its own functions.
In addition we do very extensive work for other departments, with the exception of the Department of Transport. In fact we do perform a certain amount of work for that department, but most of the construction which comes under the Department of Transport is carried on by that department itself. In the same way, construction for the Department of National Defence is carried out primarily by the Department of Defence Production. We have not yet got to the stage of building penitentiaries. I do not know whether that is a compliment or an insult, but we have not been asked as yet to do so.
Today, of course, I am dealing primarily with the construction work that my department is doing, but I would point out that defence construction during the present fiscal year is expected to reach $100 million. This is quite largely a result of the present government's policy of pushing ahead these defence
[Mr. Diefenbaker.I
projects in order to create employment. The same is true with regard to the Department of Transport. It is not my job to deal with the estimates of that department concerning construction, but they build such things as airfields, airports and ships, and I should think their expenditure during the present fiscal year will be even higher than that of the Department of Defence Production.
The Department of Public Works, in the 1958-59 estimates, is asking for approximately $218 million in the main estimates and an additional $15 million, approximately, in the supplementary estimates, making a total in round figures of $233 million. This is by far the largest sum the Department of Public Works has ever sought from parliament, and is an increase of $41.6 million over the fiscal year 1957-58.
In so far as spending money for other departments is concerned, we are being asked this year to spend $40.6 million. This amount, of course, does not appear in our own estimates but will appear in the estimates of the various departments for which we shall be doing the work. I point out that the total value of the work being undertaken by the Department of Public Works for other departments in 1958-59 is approximately $152 million. This is the value of the projects. We are actually planning to spend $40.6 million this year on these projects but the total value of the work on which we will be busy will be $152 million. That includes 236 projects, of which 168 are new items.
I have been sitting here in recent days listening to some hon. members of the opposition, for example the hon. member for Essex East, saying that nothing had been started by the government in the way of public works, that it has all been a myth.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
He did not say that; your
colleague from Newfoundland did.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
I would also point out that
the Leader of the Opposition attempted to twist the statement made by the Minister without Portfolio from Newfoundland. I heard that, too.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
The minister would be
better off looking after his estimates.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
There will be no progress
today.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
I am pointing out especially
for the benefit of hon. members of the official opposition that in the work we are doing this year for other departments there are 236 projects, of which 168 are new items.
In carrying on a public works program the department has laid down a policy of spending money in a sensible way on projects

which are needed at once or will be needed, and on projects which are the responsibility of the federal government. In other words, we have not simply gone out to put money into this project and that project for which the federal government has no responsibility whatever. One reason for that is that we think it would not make sense, and another is that there are plenty of projects which are the responsibility of the dominion government on which the money can be spent.
We have accelerated construction. This is a factor which has been almost entirely overlooked in the criticisms made from the other side of the house. For example, we have gone out of our way to promote work during the winter months. This is something which should be the objective of all governments and industries in Canada at all times, whether or not there happens to be a recession.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
This was done before under
the Liberal administration.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
That is true. This helps to
meet the seasonal nature of employment in Canada. Quoting figures for the months from October to March inclusive it is interesting to note that during the past winter the number of man hours of employment on projects of the building construction branch of the department increased 39 per cent over the comparable period in the previous year. The hours worked in 1957-58 were 3,047,000 and in the previous year, 1956-57, the hours worked were only 2,192,000. Expenditures on these projects during those winter months in 1956-57 were $18,799,000, and in 1957-58 they were up to $24,234,000.
In addition, two major winter projects were undertaken on behalf of the Department of Northern Affairs and National Resources. The first of these was the advance location survey for the national parks division to permit brushing on the Banff-Jasper-Yellowhead highway, and the second was 150 miles of brushing for the northern administration division in the Northwest Territories on the road from Providence north to Fort Rae. Location surveys were also carried out in the Wood Buffalo national park. We aim to carry on just as much work of this kind as possible during the winter months.
For several large projects the planning was advanced to permit construction to begin at much earlier dates than would normally have been the case; for example, the national film board vault building in Montreal, postal station Q in Toronto, the Post Office Department building in Ottawa, survey and mapping building in Ottawa, public buildings at Ples-sisville and Shawinigan Falls in Quebec and Burin and Harbour Buffett in Newfoundland.
Supply-Public Works
These are only some of the projects the planning for which has been rushed ahead in order that men might be put to work much earlier than would have been the case ordinarily.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: All these projects were started by the Liberal administration.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
All these projects have been rushed ahead at a rate which would have left the former administration breathless and lying on the side of the road. A large program of winter works has been undertaken in the field of building repairs. These works are not large in terms of value, but they can be done on short notice in locations where they may be required. Another advantage of these is that they are done all over the country.
The original plan for program of winter repair works had a value of $1,046,000. This program was accelerated, with the result that in the period November 1, 1957, to March 31, 1958, the works done had a value of $2,008,000; that was achieved by a special push on the contemplated works and, in addition, by bringing forward projects which otherwise would have been carried out in 1958-1959.
There has been another interesting improvement in the work of the department, and this comes to light when one considers the percentage of the estimates which has been spent.
I remember some years ago, particularly before an election, when the minister of public works of that time brought down estimates which were simply padded with items which the department had no intention of proceeding with in the fiscal year for which the estimates were tabled. I remember myself, as the opposition critic of the department at that time, referring to votes in different provinces, and it was fantastic the way those estimates had been padded for election purposes.
In the year 1957-58 some 97 per cent of the allotments has been spent, compared with 91.7 per cent in the previous year. This shows very clearly the manner in which the officials of the department have rushed ahead those piojects in order to make further work across the country. I think the figure of 97 per cent is a concrete tribute to them for the way they handled the department during those winter months.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Will the minister explain that last statement more fully? I did not catch its significance.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
In the estimates for 1958-59 a certain amount is asked for. The department tries to see that those estimates are such

Supply-Public Works
that the work will actually be carried out in the fiscal year. It is not considered to be fair to parliament, or good business, to bring in estimates for a very large amount and then spend only 60 per cent of the estimates. In the last fiscal year, 1957-58, the department has come quite near perfection in that 97 per cent of the money asked for has been spent on the projects for which the money was sought.
Then I would also like to deal with the manner in which new projects have been undertaken. These 1958-59 estimates reflect the advancement of both planning and construction in order to get an earlier start on buildings, many of which would otherwise not have been started for a year or even longer. I have some examples here; I am going to run over them quickly. Let me take Newfoundland as an example. The very first item from Newfoundland is a post office at Wesleyville, which was sought so hard by the hon. member for Bonavista-Twillingate last year, which had not been built by his own government and for which his own government had made no provision. This post office contract is now being let; the post office is to be built.
I see the leader of the C.C.F. group smiling, because he comes in exactly the same category. He has a post office at Radville, Saskatchewan, which is being built this year and which would not have been built in the ordinary course if we had not decided to accelerate every project that could be built in a businesslike way in order to help create employment. I give these two buildings as examples in answer to the chatter that is being heard in the House of Commons from some of the members of the official opposition to the effect that this work program does not mean a thing.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: How many men have been put to work under this scheme?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: I will tell the hon. member for Essex East one thing. He said nothing at all had been done. Right in his own home town we rushed ahead the demolition of old buildings on the post office site in order to create work, and we had to get around the provision made by his own government which would have prevented that demolition being carried out until much later in the year.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
You are not
putting very many to work.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: The former Liberal government did nothing at all about hurrying up this post office right in the city of the hon. member for Essex East.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: When we were in office there was no comparable unemployment.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: No unemployment? There were many warnings of coming unemployment which you carefully swept under the rug.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: That is not what the Prime Minister said last night.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
These are projects in Newfoundland which would not have been started within a year or perhaps even more had the government not deliberately gone out to make work: Wesleyville, $27,000; Deer Lake, $26,000. Harbour projects: St. John's, $12 million. The Liberal government had had a report on a harbour project for St. John's and did nothing about it. Now we have $1 million in the estimates this year. An engineering firm has been engaged to draw the plans and we are going right ahead with this work which should have been previously undertaken. It is nine or ten years since Newfoundland came into confederation. Had the former government been on its toes this project would have been undertaken many years ago. Bell Island, $100,000; Codroy, $300,000.
I now come to Nova Scotia. Here again public works projects were rushed ahead which would not have been under way this year otherwise, and certainly never would have been undertaken by the former government had it continued in power.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: There was no unemployment then.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
Digby, $150,000. Harbour projects; Caribou, $125,000; Dennis Point, $134,000; Glace Bay, $158,000; Main a Dieu, $100,000; North Sydney $158,000; Port Morien, $147,000; Port Hood, $200,000; Shelburne, $100,000.
I now come to Prince Edward Island and the Northumberland strait causeway. We got no action on that from the former government.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: What action is there now?

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
There is provision in the estimates for $360,000. An engineering firm is engaged in making a detailed survey, and if the report is favourable then the present government will proceed to construct the causeway to Prince Edward Island. In that province there is provision for a building at Borden, $26,000. Harbour projects; Alber-ton, $100,000; Fishing Cove, $85,000.
New Brunswick; here again are projects which have been rushed ahead in order to provide work this year; buildings: Campbell-ton, $250,000. Harbour projects; Buctouche, $85,000; Kennebecasis river. $150,000; Saint

John (Negro Point), $500,000; and a bridge in northern New Brunswick about which the former government did nothing for 22 years.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: We were ready.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: You were ready but you never made a move. Campbellton-Cross Point bridge; a contract has already been let for the causeway on the New Brunswick side, and the two provinces of New Brunswick and Quebec have agreed to participate in the bridge structure. It is going to cost the dominion approximately $4.2 million.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Will the minister permit a question? Has work been started on the bridge at Campbellton, and was the Minister of Transport delegated to officially inaugurate the commencement of work?

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: The contract for the causeway on the New Brunswick side was let about six weeks ago and work has actually started.

speechtext:
Was the Minister of
Transport-

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Don't you want the bridge?

speechtext:

bridge?

you members.

up your own estimates.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:

a long time.

speechtext: Turning to the province of Quebec, again these are projects under way this year which otherwise would not have been under way. Anne de Bellevue, $125,000 and a building in Ville St. Georges, $220,000. These are only the larger items.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Most of them planned before.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Then there are harbour projects at Les Eboulements, $250,000 and at Pointe au Pere or Father Point. I am surprised that the former parliamentary assistant did not get something done about the project at Father Point.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
Tell us the circumstances.
Supply-Public Works

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Other projects are at Pointe au Pic, $200,000; Riviere du Loup, $300,000; Sorel, for dredging, $135,000. Then I come to Ontario. These are projects which in most cases certainly would not have been built during the fiscal year had we not deliberately pushed ahead.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: May I ask the minister a question. Will he put on the record now how much is being spent for port facilities in Ontario as compared with Quebec?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Port facilities?

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Harbour developments, the items he has been listing.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Those were harbour items.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Would he give the total for Quebec and the total for Ontario.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: That will be in the estimates. If the hon. member will look at the book he will find it in the estimates. The hon. member is an old hand at this game. He need not try to catch me with a question like that.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: I used to be an old hand at getting my estimates through, not at holding them up.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Taking Ontario and dealing with buildings, Ottawa post office building-

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: I think we ought to give the Minister of Public Works an opportunity to tell us just how many men have been put to work under this public works program. Mr. Chairman, I am very grateful to the members of the committee. I should like to point out, however, that the hon. member for Essex East is never going to be convinced that we have put one man to

work unless we drag the poor man up here on the floor of the House of Commons. There is the new post office department building on Riverside drive in Ottawa. speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader

-it would not have been done. The amount there is $300,000. Then there is a building at Goderich, $175,000; a building at Guelph, $350,000; a building at Leamington, $310,000; a building at Oshawa, $200,000; a building at Peterborough, $200,000 and postal station F in Toronto, $750,000.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

If the members of the official opposition are not willing to give us credit for this I am sure the members of the C.C.F. group will be willing to do so.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Divide and rule.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Are they all getting post offices?

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
What is more to the point, I am sure the Canadian people will realize that we have really been trying to do something to create more jobs. Then there is the Burlington low level bridge, $4J million, which should have been undertaken long since by the former government.
[Mr. Green.l

speechtext: That was begun under the previous Liberal administration.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: This work was not begun at all, and it should have been started a long time ago.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: No, you are wrong about that.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: In Manitoba we have buildings at Portage la Prairie, $250,000 and at Winnipeg, for the unemployment insurance commission, $1,350,000. There are harbour projects at McBeth point, $62,000 and at The Pas, $90,000.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: The minister has failed to mention Fort William in the province of Ontario.

speechtext:

to announce that there is to be a new large dredge built on the west coast for the west coast, which will cost approximately $3 million.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
I am going to ask you a
lot more questions about that; don't worry.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
Those items to which I have referred are all directly the responsibility of the Department of Public Works. maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, in the 18 years during which I have been a member of this house I have never seen, on a Friday morning, such a nice floor show as has been put on today. I think the remarks the Minister of Public Works made must have been a cause of great pleasure to the officials of his department who are now sitting in the galleries and on the floor of the house, particularly when he went on to read all the items which appear under the heading of their department in this year's book of estimates. It struck me very forcibly that we witnessed

the same kind of show once before, during the past election campaign, when the Prime Minister and his colleagues promised the people of Canada that a public works program amounting to $1,185 million would be undertaken.
Well, we have witnessed the first act of this performance, and I suppose all hon. members are looking forward to seeing the second act. I did not think the minister would make the kind of statement he did. I admit I was not prepared for it. You will realize, Mr. Chairman, that because of the fact that the English language is not my own it is very difficult for me to reply immediately to all the points which were raised by the minister this morning. I am quite sure, however, that I will have another opportunity to do so during the discussion of these estimates.
This is the first occasion on which the estimates of the Department of Public Works have been brought up for discussion in committee of supply. I have before me a few words of congratulation to the minister, but I am asking myself now if it is really necessary to convey those words of congratulation to him.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Dispense.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
However, I think as a good Liberal I will congratulate him on his appointment and wish him well in his task. We have heard rumours-I do not know how true they are; they are only rumours as yet- that the hon. gentleman intends to give way to some other member of his party. I suppose that is why this morning, before leaving his office, he decided to read to the committee all the items which are included in the estimates. As a matter of fact a comment on these lines has already been made by the leader of the C.C.F. party.
I am sure we are all aware, as we were told this morning, that this department is one of the most important of the administration, and that it has grown tremendously since the end of the war. One has only to look back at the estimates of 1945, for instance, to find that the expenditures under public works for that year amounted to approximately $19 million, whereas the total expenditure incurred by the department during the fiscal year 1956-57 on its various works of construction, maintenance and operation amounted to $190 million; and this was under a Liberal administration at a time when there was no such crisis of unemployment in Canada as exists today. This comparison shows clearly how greatly the department grew and developed during a period when the economy of this country was much easier than it is today.

When in 1953, hon. Mr. Winters was appointed minister of public works, additional responsibilities were assigned to the department; the activities of Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation and also those connected with the trans-Canada highway were then placed under his jurisdiction. At this point, Mr. Chairman, I feel certain that all hon. members will agree with me when I say that Mr. Winters discharged his responsibilities with great devotion and fairness to all, having in mind as his sole aim the best interest of the Canadian people. I am sure, also, that in his new and important function he will continue to take an active part in the development of our country.
I wish to add that the growth and development of this department is also due in large measure to the able and competent civil servants who for years have worked hard and diligently to carry out their duties. I can say without hesitation that from the deputy minister down to the most humble employee I have never seen such a loyal and devoted group of men and women as those with whom I was glad to be associated from 1953 to 1957.
It is not my intention to deal at great length on this occasion with the estimates now before us. My intention was merely to make some remarks of a general nature and to inquire about any changes, new programs and new policies which the minister might be contemplating for the future. We have not heard much concerning a change in policy, nor have we seen much evidence of the initiative of the new Minister of Public Works. Practically all the items he read this morning were projects that were planned and prepared by the previous administration, as I will demonstrate later on.
Before the tabling of the estimates a lot of people in this country and many hon. members not only on the opposition side of the house but in every quarter of this chamber were expecting to see a very large increase in the amount to be spent by the Department of Public Works during the present fiscal year. In fact hon. members will recall that since the beginning of the year and particularly during the election campaign the Prime Minister and his colleagues on many occasions and at various places promised and advertised with great publicity that a vast and nation-wide program of public works would be undertaken. I am using the words of the Prime Minister: "a program of dividend-paying works of $1,185,000 would be undertaken of which $270 million would be spent in the first three months of this year."
I would have thought that in his statement this morning the Minister of Public Works
Supply-Public Works
would have told us where the sum of $270 million was spent on new projects, or does he share the view of the hon. member for St. John's West as recorded at page 758 of Hansard of June 2 this year:
Turning now to public works, I heard the hon. member for Essex East (Mr. Martin) challenge hon. members on this side of the house to say what public works-he qualified his question by adding "of a national character"-have been undertaken. He was referring to some major undertakings. Well, he knows as well as I do that no great public works of a major character has been inaugurated since this house opened, nor could it have happened before this house opened.

speakerposition: Minister Without Portfolio
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, I wonder if I could draw the attention of the hon. member for Levis to my meaning in referring to the subject raised by the hon. member for Essex East. maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
I would have thought that as a member of the cabinet the hon. member for St. John's West would have been aware of the large projects that were advertised during the election campaign. Surely this statement is of great importance to the people of Canada because it comes from one who is a member of the cabinet. Upon completion of the remarks of the hon. member for St. John's West to which I have just referred, the hon. member for Essex East is reported as saying:
If the hon. gentleman would permit me, the question I asked was: can he name a project which this government initiated which has actually been started and, if it has been started, how many men have been put to work as a result.
The hon. member for St. John's West replied:
I admit the validity of that question, and I cannot personally point to anything that has actually given great employment, but I do know of a number of works for which money will be voted in the estimates or in the supplementary estimates.
Even though the Minister of Public Works cited a long list of projects this morning we have in the above statement proof that nothing has been done in a practical way by the government to relieve the unemployment situation in Canada at this moment. As I was saying, we were expecting to see a marked increase in the amount spent by the Department of Public Works during the present fiscal year because the Prime Minister and his colleagues during the election campaign said that such expenditures would be undertaken, but we have seen nothing of the sort.

Supply-Public Works
Of course I want to be fair, and I should point out we were not expecting to find all the new projects listed in the estimates of the Department of Public Works. But on the other hand we would have thought that the building construction branch of the Department of Public Works would be spending a lot more in the present fiscal year. This morning the minister placed on the record a number of projects in an attempt to show that his is one of the most important departments of government and one which bears the responsibility of making good the promises that were made during the election campaign.
References to the vast program of public works were made during the election campaign not only by the Prime Minister but by the Minister of Public Works as well. The Ottawa Journal of January 28, 1958 reported the minister as having said in the beautiful city of Quebec, while attending the convention of the Canadian Construction Association "that the government was increasing its program of public works and was trying to build a shelf of public works projects to be carried out when employment falls off."
I remember that at the beginning of last session the minister referred to the shelf of public works that was supposed to have been prepared by the Liberal administration. "Since that time I have looked under the bed and under the sofa, and I did not find any shelf prepared by the government of which he is a member." I know a little about public works, and I challenge the minister at this time to invite me to look under the bed to find out if the government has a shelf of public works projects to relieve unemployment in the face of the serious situation that confronts us.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: Sure; you can look under the bed any time.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: I am afraid the bed is not clean.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
With more than half a million unemployed in Canada this is certainly the right time to announce a comprehensive public works program.
Referring to the estimates of the department for the present fiscal year we find that the total expenditures, including special categories-and the minister mentioned the exact figure-is $218 million compared with $175 million for the last fiscal year, or a difference of approximately $43 million. I have compared only the main estimates, of course. The increase of $43 million, it should be pointed out, is not due entirely to the initiative of this government, nor does it represent new projects solely.

If one looks at the estimates one will find there is an increase of $15 million for the trans-Canada highway. As the minister well knows that $15 million is just a matter of accounting, because that figure actually represents the amount of work that will be done by the provinces and I am not aware that he has given the provinces any additional incentive to carry on or undertake more work. There is also $5 million of the total increase which is to be charged to general administration, maintenance, operation of public buildings and grounds, and furniture and furnishings in government departments, which leaves a very small increase for new projects.
Therefore, Mr. Chairman, it seems that there is a very small increase for new projects. When one looks at the different items listed in the estimates he finds that many of them are for projects that are to be completed, and many others were planned by the previous administration. I will give an example. I am glad I made a note here, because the minister, as I said before, cited a long list of projects. I suppose it is good publicity, but I will take just one item here:
Construction, acquisition, major repairs and improvements of, and plans and sites for, public buildings.
Let me take Quebec because, of course, I am a little more familiar with my own province. There are 24 projects listed. The third one is "Chicoutimi-public building-to complete"; "Dorion-public building"; plans were prepared by the previous administration. The next item is "Hull-national printing bureau-improvements". The next item is "Montreal" and has to do with a national revenue building, another project of the previous administration. The next item is '"Montreal-postal station R-addition and alterations-to complete"; "Montreal-postal terminal-alterations and improvements". This is not a new project. Then we have the item "Montreal-vault building for national film board". This is not a new project. Then we have the item "Plessisville-public building-to complete"; the plans were prepared by the previous administration. We have the item "Quebec-Wolfe's Cove

building for customs and immigration, $2,500,000", one of the most important items of that branch to complete. Then we have "Shawinigan Falls

public building"; the plans were prepared by the previous administration. Then, "Sorel-public building"; plans also prepared by the previous administration; "Ville St. Georges-public building"; the plans were prepared by the previous administration.

This shows, Mr. Chairman, that although the minister has given a long list of items this morning we can say to him-and I suppose it would apply to some of the other departments-as far as the Department of Public Works is concerned the great majority of the items that appear in the estimates were planned by the previous administration, or they are items to complete payment for works already undertaken.
May I at this time also point out to the minister that I heard that in the fall of 1957 a number of tenders were called for different projects and for one reason or another they were put aside. I do not know how many tenders were so cancelled, but I hope when the minister replies he will give us some information regarding this question.
Now, relating the projects that appear in this year's estimates to unemployment, I wonder whether the minister will also tell us if he has received advice from the Department of Labour as to where the projects should be carried out. We all know there are some regions or districts which are affected more by unemployment than some others. Therefore I am inclined to believe that in undertaking these projects this year special attention should be given to the regions or districts that are the most affected by unemployment.
I should like at this time, Mr. Chairman, once again to bring to the attention of the minister the question of the proposed post office building in Quebec city. I must say that I was somewhat disappointed, as probably the hon. member for Quebec West and many citizens of our capital city were, that-

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: -we could not expect a start on that building this year. speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, at one o'clock before the luncheon recess I was speaking about the post office building in Quebec city and saying that I was a little disappointed that we could not expect a start this year. I also mentioned that the minister was not entirely responsible for the delay that has taken place but nevertheless I would have thought that during the eleven months the government has been in office there would have been sufficient time to iron out the difficulties between the city of Quebec and the Canadian National Railways authorities. I do not know if negotiations are still going on at this time between the two parties concerned but if not I think there is only one way to settle the question.
If the minister will permit me, I would suggest that the minister, with the help of his colleague the Minister of Transport, should arrange a meeting with the management of Canadian National Railways and try to convince them to lower the price they have been

Supply-Public Works
asking for their property. The minister and the officials of the Post Office Department must realize, as does everyone in Quebec city, that this building is badly needed, and if the minister will agree to take the step I have suggested I think he will find that the matter will be settled in the near future. (Translation):
Now, Mr. Chairman, I would like to say a few words on this matter for the benefit of Conservative members for the province of Quebec, and especially those who represent Quebec city, so that they might urge the minister to arrange for the immediate construction on this building which, as I said a moment ago, is urgently required for local postal services and which, in addition, would help to give employment to the 18,000 jobless at present in the city.
(Text):
Now, Mr. Chairman, I should like to say a few words about the trans-Canada highway. During the fiscal year 1956-57 good progress was made and if one consults the report of proceedings under the Trans-Canada Highway Act he will find on page 2 that commitments during the fiscal year totalled $82 million odd, an increase over those for the previous fiscal year of $25 million. Canada's share of 1956-57 commitments totalled $52 million, of which $11,280,000 represented payments on account of the additional 40 per cent contribution to be made to the cost of construction of 10 per cent of the highway mileage. This shows that the amendment brought down by the previous administration and approved by the house early in 1956 has had the expected effect of accelerating the rate of construction.
Hon. members will also recall that when the amendment was discussed in the house our friends now sitting opposite were very critical of the progress that had been made. They were also blaming the government of the day for not paying at least 90 per cent of the total cost of the road. I could read from Hansard many statements that have been made, particularly by the hon. member for Victoria and also supported by many other members of the Conservative party of that time. If we look at item 366 of the estimates for this year we find that the amount provided for the construction of the highway through national parks, for which the minister knows the federal government is entirely responsible, shows a decrease of $500,000. Unless the amount of $12,500,000 appearing in the estimates represents the money required to complete all of the roads within the national parks I do not think that the present government has reason to say, as the minister said so often this morning, that they are doing a better job than the previous administration.
[Mr. Bourget.l

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext: He was just kidding.

maintopic: REPORTED RESOLUTION OF FEDERATION OF MAYORS AND MUNICIPALITIES
speechtext:
In any event, the minister is now in a position to change the policy that was followed up to June, 1957, and when he answers I hope he will take the opportunity to explain to the committee the changes he has in mind so as to fulfil the promises made by his party when they were in opposition.
At this point I should also like to ask-the hon. member for Victoria (Ont.) also inquired about this some years ago-if the minister has made any approach to the government of the province of Quebec so as to convince them to share in this program if it is not too late. We Liberals, I think, have reason to regret that our province did not take advantage of this project, thus losing since 1949 from $25 million to $30 million which we all know could be so well used at the present time in the province of Quebec, particularly for education. I hope that the minister, with the help of his numerous colleagues now surrounding him-

speechtext:
